title: Netherlands: flood, storm, or having to leave home
short: The Dutch government's flood and extreme-weather pages, and leaving home with your kit
intro: What the Dutch government's pages say to think about before a flood or severe storm, what to do in a red weather warning, and what to have ready if you have to leave your home. Shown only in a library that holds the Netherlands documents.

choices.label: Floods could reach my area: what should I do ahead of time?
choices.hint: Dry places, escape routes, the gas valve, neighbours, animals

read.label: Flooding: think ahead
read.note: Check overstroomik.nl, pick the place that stays dry longest, check escape routes, know the main gas valve, keep blankets dry, plan for animals and neighbours.

read.label: The emergency kit you can take with you
read.note: The one-page kit list; the flooding page says to take the kit with you if you have to leave.

choices.label: I may have to leave my home
choices.hint: Where to go, what to take, getting out if the front door is blocked

read.label: Flooding: where to go, what to take, how to get out
read.note: Think in advance whom you can go to, take the kit, check exits such as a skylight or ladder, and see whether animals can come to a dry place.

read.label: Keep a bag ready for a sudden departure
read.note: Step 5 of the booklet's kit steps: a bag ready to put things in if you suddenly have to leave.

read.label: Plan form: how to get out safely, and where to meet
read.note: Questions to answer with your household: another way out, an agreed meeting place and address, and two emergency contacts.

choices.label: A severe storm or a red weather warning
choices.hint: Code red, going out, calling for help

read.label: Extreme weather: during a code red and what to prepare
read.note: Stay at home on code red if you can; if you must go out take food, drink, a blanket and a phone with charger and say where you are going.

choices.label: How will I be warned, and where do I find news?

read.label: NL-Alert
read.note: A message to your phone when there is an incident near you; it works when the network is overloaded.

read.label: The siren
read.note: Outside the monthly test, go inside, close windows, doors and other openings, and follow the news.

read.label: Regional radio when power and internet fail
read.note: A battery or DAB+ radio with FM can still get the regional broadcaster; the frequency list is on the next page.

limits.text: During a code red weather alarm, stay at home if you can; if you have to go out, tell others where you are going and by which route.
Only call 112 for a life-threatening situation. For the fire brigade without an emergency, such as storm damage or flooding, the page gives 0900-0904.
The flooding page's check of whether your house is at risk is on overstroomik.nl, a website in Dutch only.

prepare.label: Flooding: government actions, and the page's own checklist
prepare.note: Dunes, dams and dykes keep the water out; the page lists what the government does and what households can do.

prepare.label: Floods in Limburg: neighbours who helped
prepare.note: In the booklet's "Helping each other" section, residents gave boots, coffee and towels to people who had to leave their homes.

learn.label: Denk vooruit web pages: alerts, flooding, power, water, weather (text-only edition)
learn.note: Nine pages copied from the government's Denk vooruit site, including flooding and extreme weather.
